analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop.swift head lines 1-1143. The changes are limited to stored-state declarations: the autopilotHistory tuple gains labels and a detail field (head 342-343), and new autopilot placement/watchdog state is added (head 355-380): autopilotAdoptedModelIDs, autopilotHolds, autopilotBusyClock, transitionWatchdog, autopilotStalledCommandId, startupPreloadStopRequested, startupPreloadCandidate, resliceGateGeneration and transitionGenerations. No crypto, attestation, key, encryption or send-path logic changed in this file. SendHandle flush ordering, keyPair generation (A-003) and signer selection are unchanged.

The added test file AutopilotAdoptionTests.swift is only visible through its patch excerpt. Its metadata has no citable head side, so no line can be cited. The excerpt shows a new behavior: after the autopilot lease ends, an adopted inventory model stays advertised and servable without a lease (autopilotServesModel true, autopilotAllowsModel false). It is admitted through ensureModelLoaded and fastAdmissionReject.

Integration must verify the implementation in ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement (not supplied) for three properties:
(a) An adopted model's weight hash is recorded in modelHashes/liveModelHashes and attested, so per-model hash verification is not bypassed (T-012, T-027, A-004).
(b) Adoption cannot re-advertise a build that failed its self-test or is tombstoned (failedSelfTestHashes, retiringModels).
(c) Adoption is triggered only by coordinator-authorized operations and is cleared on disconnect, update or revocation. This matters for stale serving authority under T-053.

The autopilotInventoryModels filter (head 821-824) requires a non-empty weightHash, which partially supports (a). The new detail strings in autopilotHistory may be reported to the coordinator; check that they do not include prompt data (A-001). No regression is evident in the supplied source.
